title: Panel: Natural Graphite’s Role in Tier‑1 Anode Supply
gist: This is a member-only video page for a Benchmark Summit 2026 London panel on natural graphite's role in tier-1 anode supply, with Talga founder Mark Thomspon and Benchmark head of consulting Shruti Kashyap. The page gives only the framing that graphite is the supply chain's weak link, that anodes are the next battleground, and that it is unclear whether the West can scale anode supply.

insights.claim: A Benchmark Summit 2026 London session on natural graphite's role in tier-1 anode supply framed graphite as the overlooked anode material and the weak link in the battery supply chain.
insights.speaker: Mark Thomspon, Founder and Managing Director, Talga; Shruti Kashyap, Head of Consulting, Benchmark
insights.so_what: If graphite is the binding constraint, anode-material suppliers outside China may get pricing power and policy support.
insights.quote: The overlooked anode: why graphite is the supply chain's weak link

insights.claim: The graphite session asked whether the West can scale anode supply to break the graphite bottleneck; the page leaves the question open and gives no answer.

insights.so_what: Western anode capacity build-out is an open question, so execution risk for non-Chinese graphite and anode projects stays high.
